name: Humanoid robots in structured industrial work
summary: Human-shaped robots attempt useful physical tasks in factories and warehouses designed around people.
useCase: A humanoid repeatedly moves standardized totes between a fixed station and a conveyor, with measured uptime and a safe escalation process.
whyNow: Actuators, perception and robot-learning systems are improving, and some suppliers now disclose revenue and customer trials. UBTECH’s full-size humanoid products and services revenue rose from RMB35.6 million in 2024 to RMB820.6 million in 2025. BMW described a 2025 Figure pilot involving roughly 1,250 operating hours. Neither figure proves broad economical autonomy across a full factory shift.

mainstream.scope: Repeatable, narrowly specified tasks in structured factories and warehouses, with human support and controlled operating areas.
mainstream.rationale: Real customer trials and early revenue make industrial niches plausible by 2035. Reliability, safety, maintenance and labor-equivalent cost remain unproven at broad scale. A credible downside is that adoption remains a niche beyond 2035 or is displaced by cheaper robot arms and wheeled systems. General-purpose household robots are outside this forecast.

metric.name: UBTECH full-size humanoid products and services revenue
metric.scope: UBTECH’s disclosed full-size embodied-intelligence humanoid business; one supplier.
metric.limitations: Company-specific revenue from a very small base, including products and services. Sales may include research, demonstration or government customers rather than sustained productive industrial use. The 2026 annual result is not yet available; first-half revenue is not substituted. The annual-report PDF was verified via its indexed HKEX filing; direct extraction exceeded retrieval size limits.
metric.futureNote: Do not extrapolate the early 23× increase. Factory capacity, conditional orders and planned shipments are not realized sales or productive robot hours. The forward maturity path is explicitly conditional.

outlookMetrics.name: Agility RoboFab designed annual capacity
outlookMetrics.scope: Factory design capacity at full utilization
outlookMetrics.note: A designed capacity ceiling disclosed in September 2026, not robots produced, shipped or sold. No date for reaching full utilization is assumed.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: Hyundai completed a controlling investment in Boston Dynamics, illustrating incumbent interest in advanced robotics.
No defensible industry-wide commercial deployment count identified.
No consistent production-hour or revenue series for the whole humanoid industry identified.
UBTECH reported RMB35.6 million of full-size humanoid products and services revenue.
UBTECH’s category revenue reached RMB820.6 million; BMW’s Figure pilot accumulated about 1,250 operating hours.
Agility unveiled Digit 5 and continued its proposed public transaction; BMW introduced another industrial humanoid trial in Leipzig.

tailwinds: A human-compatible form can access some existing tools and spaces without a full factory redesign.
Learning systems and simulation may lower the cost of teaching repetitive manipulation tasks.
bottlenecks: Dexterity, battery endurance, falls, maintenance and safe proximity to people remain difficult.
Purpose-built arms and mobile robots may deliver better economics; supplier orders can be conditional and capacity announcements speculative.
watchMetrics: Paid productive hours per robot, intervention frequency, uptime and independently measured cost per completed task.
Repeat orders from operating customers, including service costs and comparison with simpler automation alternatives.
